added_provisions.reason: The map rests the whole document list on the search duty in rule (17)(a) of section 31 of the Notaries Ordinance but omits the proviso that closes rule (17), under which the parties may authorise the notary in writing to dispense with the search. The duty is qualified, and the qualification belongs in the map. Added as a supporting provision with a qualifies edge from PROV-M052-001 and cited by CL-M052-Q01-001.

Section 3(2) of the Land Reform Law vests only the excess held at the commencement of the Law in 1972. Section 5(1), which the map omitted, is what makes the fifty-acre ceiling operate against a person who becomes an owner afterwards, and so is what justifies calling for landholding declarations in a 2021 purchase. Added as a supporting provision with a qualifies edge from PROV-M052-015 and cited by CL-M052-Q01-022.

question_decisions.note: All eight indispensable provisions verified, so no downgrade is triggered. statute_only is retained: the gaps in the answer are non-corpus statutes and conveyancing practice, not Roman-Dutch doctrine or case law, and no claim in the answer depends on a judgment. Four claims are marked disputed for under-support or temporal wording, and the completeness of the document list against exam practice is referred to the lawyer as a disagreement rather than resolved here.

disagreements.researcher_position: The document list may be confined to items traceable to a corpus provision, with the practice items (thirty-year search, local-authority street line and building line certificates, non-vesting certificate, tax clearance) recorded in corpus_gaps, and the question still scored as statute_only proposed_gold.
disagreements.verifier_position: statute_only is right on the prompt test, because nothing in the answer needs case law or Roman-Dutch doctrine. But a four-mark examination answer on documents to call for on a rubber estate would be marked against the practice list, and a gold answer that silently drops those items risks penalising a correct model answer. The lawyer should decide whether the omitted practice items belong in the gold answer or whether the question should be reserved until the Partition Act, the Pradeshiya Sabhas Act and the Inland Revenue Act are in the corpus.

disagreements.researcher_position: PROV-M052-003 (Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (16)(a)) and PROV-M052-007 (Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2) carry applicable_to_matter_date true, on the footing that the underlying requirement pre-dates the matter even though the quoted wording was substituted after it.
disagreements.verifier_position: The excerpts are verbatim, but they are post-2022 text. applicable_to_matter_date describes the text quoted, not the underlying policy, so on both entries it should read false with the substance carried in the temporal note. Both are marked partially_verified. The map convention should be settled once for the whole run, because PROV-M052-019 and PROV-M052-020 use false for the same situation.

unsupported_claims: CL-M052-Q01-015: the chain-of-deeds limb is supported by PROV-M052-002 and PROV-M052-007, but the trailing words about calling for any testamentary or partition proceedings have no corpus provision behind them; the Partition Act is not in the corpus and neither the Notaries Ordinance rule (33) nor the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance mentions devolution proceedings. Marked disputed.

CL-M052-Q01-017: nothing in the corpus supports the proposition that a registered mortgage entry survives repayment until a discharge is executed. Grep over the Registration of Documents Ordinance for discharge and over the Mortgage Act for extinguished returned no match. Section 7 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance is a priority rule and does not carry the claim. Marked disputed.

CL-M052-Q01-023: the certificate of incorporation, articles, share register and register of directors and secretaries are supported by section 120 of the Companies Act, but the board resolution authorising the purchase is not. The only corpus authority for a board resolution is rule (14) of section 31 of the Notaries Ordinance, whose corporate-body wording was substituted by Act No. 31 of 2022, after the matter date. Marked disputed.

missing_definitions_or_exceptions: Proviso to rule (17) of section 31 of the Notaries Ordinance: the parties may authorise the notary in writing to dispense with the search. Added as PROV-M052-901.
Section 5(1) of the Land Reform Law: the ceiling bites on a person who becomes an owner after 1972, which section 3(2) alone does not do. Added as PROV-M052-902.

Section 3 of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act (exemptions from section 2) is not in the map. It does not change the outcome on these facts, since the purchaser is a Sri Lankan company below the fifty per cent threshold, but section 2(1) is expressly subject to it and a complete map of that limb should record it.

Section 66 of the Land Reform Law defines agricultural land and expressly reaches private lands and things attached to the earth, which is what brings a rubber estate inside the ceiling. The map applies the ceiling without citing the definition.

Rule (30) of section 31 of the Notaries Ordinance (keep a true copy of the power of attorney with the protocol and forward a copy to the Registrar of Lands) is at-matter-date authority for calling for a power of attorney. The map treats the power of attorney as unsupported at the matter date because it looked only at section 3 of the Powers of Attorney Ordinance, whose corpus text is post-2022.

Section 2(2)(a) of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act requires foreign shareholding to stay below fifty per cent for twenty years, and section 4(4)(a) requires six-monthly certificates from the company secretary. Neither is a document to call for before the transfer, but both bear on the advice that surrounds the secretary's certificate in CL-M052-Q01-024.
case_law_dependence: None. No claim in the answer turns on a judgment, and the answer prose cites no case. The prescription limb (CL-M052-Q01-008 and CL-M052-Q01-019) is stated at the level of section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance and does not reach into the case law on the nature of adverse possession, which is where case law would become indispensable.
enrichment_issues: No statute name, section number or conclusion is leaked in the enriched background.

The phrase describing the Singaporean shareholder as not a citizen of Sri Lanka tracks the statutory definition of foreigner in section 25 of the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act closely enough to signpost that Act. Stating his nationality plainly would carry the same fact with less signposting.

FACT-M052-Q01-006 (the neighbour in possession of two acres for fifteen years) adds a prescription issue that the original four-mark question did not contain. It extends the document list rather than replacing the issue, so it is within the enrichment rule, but it is the added fact most likely to be judged as changing the question and should be put to the lawyer.
